paragraphs: Here's what this passage teaches, friend. God told Moses to speak to the rock, and Moses struck it twice. The water still gushed out, so the rock did its job. But the LORD said, "Because you did not trust Me to show My holiness in the sight of the Israelites, you will not bring this assembly into the land that I have given them." (Numbers 20:12)

So the problem wasn't the water. It was trust. I think the people's quarreling and Moses' anger piled up until he stopped leaning on what God said and leaned on what he could do with his own hands. I know that move. I've tried to fix a crooked cookie by pressing harder, and all I got was a bigger mess. The LORD's way was simpler than ours, and it was enough.

Now here's why this matters to you. Obeying God means doing what He said, the way He said it, and trusting Him to do the rest. Even a faithful servant like Moses felt the weight of a mistake, so let it make you careful and let it make you humble. And look at verse 13: Meribah is where Israelites quarreled with the LORD, "and He showed His holiness among them." God stayed holy and kept providing, even in the middle of all that mess, and that's the kind of God you can trust.
